objective: Prove or disprove the hinge: can a HOST-plane plugin resolve and drive the compaction engine that serves member sessions (a preset isolate realm)? Plus: member id -> live Agent, inject safety, and a minimal end-to-end drive with a busy control.

isolatedBoot.shape: DSH_HOME=<mkdtemp> + HOME=<mkdtemp> + workspace=<mkdtemp>/ws, profile mpd-headless installed from this checkout, then a REAL dsh boot
isolatedBoot.credentialBoundary: This environment has no provider key, so every boot ends with `dsh: MISSING_CREDENTIAL: llm-deepseek ...` (exit 1). That is a property of the environment, NOT of the probe: the boot got far enough to create a real session and register a live idle Agent (observed), which is what the hinge needs. No boot produced an apply/schema crash signature.

criterion1_hinge.statement: A host-plane plugin CAN reach a compaction engine with a callable compactNow, but the reaching differs by path; the engine that serves a member session is the one on the MEMBER'S scoped context.

observations.hostPlaneServiceWithoutInject: `ctx.get("compaction")` at apply time returned undefined (variant A) — the service is not synchronously present for an inject-free host row.
observations.hostPlaneServiceWithInject: With `inject: ["compaction"]` (variant B) the same lookup returned an OBJECT with `compactNow` of type function at apply time. So the host plane DOES have a compaction service; the loader defers the row until it exists.
observations.memberScopedEngine: `ctx.agents.get(<memberId>).ctx.get("compaction")` returned an OBJECT whose `compactNow` is a function — resolved in BOTH variants and with NO inject declaration.
observations.identity: The two resolved engines are NOT the same object (`sameObject: false`) while both report `name: "compaction"` and carry the same keys (`ctx, name, config, warnedPressureConfigTargets, overflowRetries, overflowAgents`). Each realm therefore exposes its own `BasicCompactionEngine` instance under the same service name.
observations.callPathReachesTheEngine: A real `compactNow(agent, signal)` against the member-scoped engine returned `null` — which the shipped source documents as 'no safe useful range exists'. It did NOT throw `busy` and did NOT crash, so the call travelled the whole path into `selectCompactableRange` and answered.

criterion1_hinge.whyNullNotSuccess: The shipped selector returns null when the session has no priced nodes. The isolated headless session cannot accumulate content (no provider key ⇒ no model turn), so a non-null compaction is not reachable in this environment. Recorded as a limit, not dressed up as success.
criterion1_hinge.designConclusion: The planned plugin must drive the engine through the MEMBER's scoped context (`agent.ctx.get("compaction")`), never through a host-plane `ctx.get("compaction")`: the host instance is a different object and would target the wrong realm.

observation.lookup: ctx.agents.list() returned exactly one live agent; its id is the shared session/agent id (session-19d8a7a3-…).
observation.note: Session exposes `log` + `eventsSnapshot` (no top-level `read`), which is how a durable-drive observer should look for `compaction/start`/`compaction/end`.

criterion2_memberToLiveAgent.stagedCase: Not exercised in this pass: the staged-not-yet-spawned shape (`members[].id === ""`) belongs to the agent-teams record and does not arise in a single-session boot. The implication is recorded from the plugin's own contract, not measured here: a staged team has no live agent, so it cannot be compacted.

a_injectEmpty.measured: variant A mounted and applied cleanly with `inject: []`; no crash signature; no pending loader entry; the plugin then resolved the service lazily later (the probe's retry loop is the pattern a lazy plugin would need).
a_injectEmpty.degradation: Because `ctx.get('compaction')` answered undefined at apply time and the platform never signalled the service, an inject-free host plugin must poll/retry to notice the engine. A plugin that assumed availability at apply would silently never compact.

b_injectDeclared.measured: variant B declared `inject: ["compaction"]` in a composition where the compaction GROUP lives in the preset plane. The boot produced NO pending loader entry and NO crash; the row applied only once the service existed, and the lookup then resolved.
b_injectDeclared.expectedByContract: The task contract anticipated that declaring the inject might leave the loader entry pending or take the tree down when no compaction plane exists.
b_injectDeclared.result: CONTRADICTED in this configuration: it did neither. The host plane owns a compaction service instance, so the declared inject is satisfiable and the row simply defers.

criterion3_injectSafety.guidanceForTheNewPlugin: Prefer `inject: ["compaction"]` for the host-plane row: availability then gates the apply deterministically, with no polling race, and the measured cost is zero (no pending entry, no crash). If the plugin must also tolerate a composition WITHOUT any compaction service, keep the lookup defensive and degrade with a warning instead of assuming the seam.

criterion4_endToEnd.verdict: PARTIALLY PROVEN — the call path is driven, the success value is not reachable in this environment

driveCall.interpretation: documented 'no safe useful range' for a content-free session

busyNegativeControl.expectedByContract: a second call on a non-idle member must yield the `busy` failure code
busyNegativeControl.measured: the concurrent second call threw `Error: cannot get required service "tokenMeter" in inactive context` (no ManualCompactionError, no `busy` code)
busyNegativeControl.assessment: The expected busy code was NOT observed. The thrown text names a Cordis lifecycle problem (an inactive context still holding a required-service lookup) rather than the idle-agent guard. This is recorded as a CONTRADICTION of the criterion's expectation, not smoothed over.
busyNegativeControl.consequence: Two things the design must not assume: (i) that a concurrent drive necessarily surfaces `busy`; (ii) that the engine can be called from a context whose lifecycle has moved on. The drive must be issued from a live context and must handle this error class explicitly.

criterion4_endToEnd.observabilityLimit: `compaction/start` and `compaction/end` could not be observed because no non-null compaction ran: the isolated session held no priced nodes, and generating content requires a provider key this environment does not have. A durable-event assertion is therefore still owed, and it needs a credentialed boot.

criterion5_alternativeIfDisproven.verdict: NOT TRIGGERED (the hinge was not disproven)
criterion5_alternativeIfDisproven.reservedPlan: Had the agent-scoped engine been unreachable, the fallback was to place the row inside the preset's compaction group. The preset declares `isolate: { compaction: true, toolResultPruner: true }` around the compaction group (presets/mpd/agent.cordis.yml:275-280), whose children are `dsh-compaction-basic` and the command row — i.e. the realm that owns the member-facing engine. The measured `sameObject: false` supports that reading, but the realm placement was not exercised and remains untested.
criterion5_alternativeIfDisproven.note: The finding that the agent-scoped engine resolves from the host plane makes the fallback unnecessary, but the row-placement question is still open for the owner of that composition.

rawEvidence: raw/probe-inject-none.jsonl (variant A: host lookup undefined, agent-scoped engine resolved)
raw/probe-inject-declared.jsonl (variant B: host lookup resolved after deferral)
raw/probe-drive.jsonl (identity comparison, fields, real compactNow call, concurrent control)

criterion7_isolationAndNeutrality.productFilesTouched: none — `git status` shows no tracked change outside evidence/omo-align/compact-hinge/
criterion7_isolationAndNeutrality.neutrality: no withdrawn external-project identifier appears in this evidence

recommendationForTheOwner: Build the host-plane plugin with `inject: ["compaction"]` (measured safe) and resolve the MEMBER engine per agent via `agent.ctx.get("compaction")`; never call a host-plane `ctx.get("compaction")` for a member.
Gate the drive on a live agent: a staged team has no agent id, so it cannot be compacted — assert `agent` exists before attempting, and treat the empty-id case as 'not yet compactable'.
Do NOT assume `busy` is the failure signal for a concurrent drive; handle the inactive-context/tokenMeter error class explicitly and re-issue from a live context.
Treat a `null` return as 'no safe useful range' (documented) rather than an error, and record it in the audit.
A credentialed end-to-end pass is still owed to assert the durable `compaction/start`/`compaction/end` pair and a non-null result.
knownLimits: No provider key in this environment: no model turn, therefore no priced session content, therefore no non-null compaction and no durable event pair.
The busy control was taken concurrently with the first call rather than against a genuinely mid-turn agent; it yielded a lifecycle error, so the true busy path remains unmeasured.
The preset-plane row-placement fallback was reasoned from the composition and the measured object identity, not exercised.
